newsitem.title: USA: Ortho-McNeil says FDA clears seizure drug. [CORRECTED 13:13 GMT 28/12]
newsitem.headline: Ortho-McNeil says FDA clears seizure drug. [CORRECTED 13:13 GMT 28/12]

text.p: (Corrects spelling of drug throughout from "Topomax" to "Topamax".)

Johnson & Johnson unit Ortho-McNeil Pharmaceutical said Friday it received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market Topamax, an antiepileptic drug used to reduce seizure freqency.

The company said Topamax was an adjunctive therapy for parital onset seizures, the most common type of seizures afflicting adults. It said it was particulary effective in patients not controlled by (corrects from "not using") other antiepileptic drugs.

Topamax was discovered and developed by the R.W. Johnson Pharmaceutical Research Institute and would be marketed in the United States by Ortho-McNeil, the company said. Both companies were units of Johnson & Johnson.
The drug is already marketed in Britain, Sweden and South Africa and is awaiting regulatory approval in 20 other countries, it said.
